And My Life... [finally I did put it into words!]

September 25, 2005

Itchy titchy, but sure Bitchy! And that’s how life is! :-) Well, I am not here to boast about how tough my life has been or to acquire anyone’s amplified sympathy; instead at this point I would say that reasons for this “so called public” confession are not clear to myself.

I have always wondered that how and when people start to feel the need to document our lives? Even a bigger question is “Why at all?” Aren’t we happy that our lives are a black box secret after all? Aren’t we content with the fact that no one knows about the dark side of that “decaying” smile? I have never been able to answer this question myself. Yeah… myself. I have never been a person of general discussions; I am one of those loners, who worked all alone in his life. And no matter what I have achieved in my life, good or bad, it is purely a result of my own capabilities, instincts and choices. At least look at the positive side; I can’t blame you for anything!!

Well, it is going to be a long story which does not have any names but only people in it. People who mean to me a lot more than just names. And trust me, if you are reading it, then it’s just because I have gathered enough courage to trust you with my secret, or rather secrets. There are things in here, which will leave you “mouth-wide-open”. Yes, my life has been ugly, and that carefully contrived smile on my face, has no connection whatsoever to the “dark-side”!

It starts like any other family story, with parents and their two kids. I am the youngest, and one who was supposed to be most spoiled and one who was suppose to grow up that way; so that I could vanish all the minted coins of my father on my whims and fancies, exactly the way, most of my cousin brothers and sisters do. Anyway, it never happened, instead my life turned into a skid mark with a burning smell of rubber. I hate that smell, not only it makes me puke but also it kills off all the good brain cells in my head. At least that’s the idea that my ingenious mind conceived, after years of brooding and manipulation. I have never felt any smarter after inhaling that choking and worthless smoke; instead I have had that “dumb” feeling for actually inhaling it! Well, I must be right then!

Now, if we would just zap back into time, 13 years back. [I have lost the count invariably.] You would see a family of four, blooming, in that small countryside town. We had it all. Yes, we had all the love, we had all the peace and we had all the smiles we needed to live by.
I was as young as almost 11 years old. Not too much of age to be truthful. I had seen enough by that time. I had seen my dad’s amazing grin when he became important political figure, with his own rules and principals. I am not here to tell how honest and character oriented person he was, all I have to say is that he was good enough for common man to support and adore him; and good enough for his corrupt opposition to hate him for his guts. He’s seen life. And along with him, we all did. I remember when he got framed for a murder he never committed. Yeah… politics can be really ugly, especially when you don’t let politics be “politics”. He told me all about the chilling nights he spent hiding in sugarcane/paddy fields without anything to cover himself, while closest of his friends, tried best to gather proofs of his innocence. Well, trauma and humiliation came to end, when real convict was caught and trialed. Each night my mom cried herself to sleep and sometimes, she just cried. I was too busy too build castles of G.I.Joe and Hot-wheels. For me, it was just another year of school.
I vividly remember, soon after that, how the hundu-muslim riots had broken out and whole town was thirsty for each other’s blood. With all man in house, posted on terrace, doing air firing, it was just a hooligan festival that no one seemed to enjoy. My dad was posted on my house terrace with rifle, to scare away, all those who tried to break into my house; while “the family” sneaked through connecting neighborhood windows to the hidden basement of a temple, owned by us. With lips dry and throat choking with tears, I don’t have any other vivid memory, when I was so petrified. There were moments that day, when I truly believed that I am not going to make it. In fact none of us is going to make it! All women and children, having locked themselves into largest room in temple, just survived that night of confronting gunshots with the assuring sound of each other’s breath. In those moments of desperation, my dad and his rifle were something that instilled hope; and that hope was based on the fact, that, that rifle had power to take all the hopes from someone else’s life. Did I not mention already, life could be ironical?

Well, this is not even beginning. I haven’t started. Mind me, when I said, all this time, a family of four was blooming all the way to glory and certainly it was.

I had never seen my mother cry so hard. All I knew that, on an unexpected day-off taken from school, something must have been truly wrong. I still remember, her hugs of despair, which just squeezed the remaining life out of me; as if one trying to transfer part of my life while you pray for another. My dad had met a severe accident; he was thought to be dead and left on roadside, covered under a sheet. Hours went by, before [coincidently] one of my uncle passed by. He was shocked to see him there. He was a doctor and it was pretty clear, that the survival chances were grim as injury was on head. Blood loss was immense. What added to the “thrill” that a suitable hospital to handle that kind of emergency was neat 300 kms away. I don’t know who drove the car that day; I just thank him with whole of my heart.
While everyone zapped away with a body as good as gone, I was sinking in the news, on a fork split road, which divided into two ways. One way to hospital, that my dad already undertook, and other one to home. Which was just “house” without him?
Two months of comma “in” ICU; my dad. Two months of comma “outside” ICU; my mom. She has always stayed by his side, and she did that in his most deserted hour too. Life support system pumping life along with enduring prayers from my mom. He did live to tell his story. He lived because he never “smoked”; he lived because he never touched “liquor” and he lived because we all desperately needed him. And yet he lived only after an attack of brain hammeroage, paralysis of right side of body and complete memory loss.
For then, my mom and sister were just nurses, doctors were doctors and friends were strangers. Me? I was still his son!! Yes, and that’s all he remembered. I was eleven that time and yet somehow I knew how compelling true love is. What power it has to defy the logic and sanity of science. And that singular memory of me was the best gift a father could give to his son.
He couldn’t speak. He would see four images of everything. He couldn’t walk. He couldn’t do anything, of practical usability that would add to the help of my mom, while she winded up with daily chores for him. Yet I remember those beady eye-balls full of questions, those evident frowns for all the faces around and most of all, the most brilliant smile that would surge up on his face immediately, as soon as I came near to him.

I was the proud witness of moments, when he failed his “fluid injection system” by drinking milk glass all by himself, just because I asked him to! Well, doctors were stunned, and I was just starting to realize the amount of determination he has behind that impenetrable face.
He recovered, and he recovered against all the predictions made by meds. But heavy antibiotics had done their job. His triggered emotions would come out as intense anger and tears that couldn’t be helped. A man, who saw it all without a single bead of tear; cries for min 8 sec now, when he hears my voice on phone each time. Apart from emotion triggering, the weight; he loathes it, but he can’t exercise to loose it. Yes, life can be frustrating.
My mom has been a silent spectator always. She has boundless perseverance and limitless endurance. Something, I didn’t inherit from her. Her, strong faith has always shown results and I somehow know, it always will. She’s a woman of belief.

Whole family survived through all this, banking on self-sustaining yet declining business. My dad saw through few smaller accidents, where he broke his arm bone and had steel rods put into it. Almost lost his leg due to infection and other minor injuries and accident, at least they looked minor now.

While this was one part of life, there were other dimensions too. For instance, my sister found her soul mate and no matter how much, my parents disliked her choice, she was determined to be heard and married to man she thought to be right and perfect for her. I was the only one, on her side, but only because I liked her. My mistake! L

It’s funny that how people in such a small town with stereotype life, always have something to gossip about, and what is equally not funny, is that how relatives suddenly crave for all the money they can lay their hands on with or without concern for, whom does it belong to? Yes, I wasn’t blessed with best of the relatives that way. And probably in movies, you can’t lay hands on the sprawling estates and hard earned property of a man who knew how to fight for himself, but who is just too weak to stand up against anyone, anymore; in real life YES YOU CAN!

All the brotherly love and concern are just mocking words, hollow and deprived of love. The entire place is taken by greed. And what is more disturbing is the fact that how ugly greed can make you. Threats, attempts to assault and other things of similar nature are just way too common.

Few years prior to these happenings, I had shifted to other city for making a bright career, because my foresighted mother did not see a future for me, among a pack of wolves that were living for the smell of minted coins. Yes, probably it’s the smell of minted coins and not printed books that drive this world. I should have known that.

I was not told about all the happenings, not by my family at least. It was only through my cousins, who had a habit of prying over their parent’s mature conversations, that I came to know of all this, later on. I have lived those moments of helplessness, with “I-will-kill-them-all-one-day” feeling. Somewhere inside, that savage is still lurking and planning.

My sister got married with all due and deserved pampering and love, to a guy, she dreamed of day and night. But throughout, I could see it very evidently on my mom’s face that, among those lines of responsibilities, there was a line hidden, which just spoke of disappointment. And I have learned one thing in my life. “Never ever question mother’s instincts”

So now my family was divided into groups. I was fighting my way up. My sister was getting a hang of life, full of responsibilities. And my parents fighting away the herd of wolf pack, which were after all the money and property my dad had made in prime of his life. And not surprisingly, they were soon to be joined by my parent’s own son-in-law. [Now let me say this at this point: SonOfABitch]

I was coping up with life, but pressure shows on your face at the end of the day. In those blessed days of school hostel, I learned a new way to live my life. Split personality. Yes, and that is what I am. The decaying me who keeps all the “dirty logs” of life buried in pages and in heart. The humorous me, who is a wrapper to my true self and interface to whole world. Those two years of final school life did the trick. I was as impenetrable as I ever wanted to be. Of all the cute faces, I found only one face I instantly fell for. Com’on, you think I am “dare-to-do-it” type? Now, maybe I am; but those days I was not. I completed my school life without speaking a single line of meaningful words to her. Assumed to be infatuation, I decided to just let her pass by as a rare fragrance of no vital importance.

Nurturing a dream of becoming a world-renowned businessman! I gave it all up to pursue a “secure” future in “Engineering”. And well, I fared well enough. Closely related with computers I was happy and content. I have been always optimistic about life, and as it happens, it always turns out for good at the end. I was blessed with nephew, my mom and dad with grandson. Finally it hit me; I am on my way to better days. Finally. Years had passed, since I felt that kind of enthusiasm among us. He was the bond who was going to hold each other.
I met the “no-talk-girl-of-school” on net one day. She became my best friend ever. She IS my best friend ever. What you “can’t” get out of me in years, she can make me talk in “5 minutes” flat. All she has to do is talk to me. Well, things were brightening up. But as very truly said, “Dreams have a habit of going bad, when you are not looking at them”.

My sister’s marriage was breaking up. My brother in law closed the small whatever enterprise he was given by my parents; in hope to lay his hands on my dad’s business. His family had lost all theirs already owing to obscured reasons. So my sister decided to split. He wouldn’t. Because that would have taken his last chance to have all that he dreamed of.

Living single with a kid when you are married and hold yourself in dignity and high self esteem, by not taking anyone’s help, including your very own brother; is not a very lucrative life to live. The trauma and pressure kind of dawns on you. You turn into this vessel, which tries to hold more water than what it actually can. Now and then, it would slip off the edges. It is very hard life to live. And only thing which is harder in nature is the question that a kid of small age can come up about his missing parent.

Letting all the dearest things go is not easy in life. When after 3 years of non stop brooding and nagging thoughts you realize that what you have for someone in heart is just little more than infatuation, then it becomes more of a dilemma rather than a choice. But nothing lasts forever. [Yeah…golden rule]
She was off for some obscure reasons. Obscure to you at least. And I was at square one, wondering what could I have done to prevent it? Probably nothing! else I would have already done it. :-D

I had already secured a safe job and was into it, with all my heart and soul. I believed that if I was true to my work and if I worked hard enough, success is all mine to relish. But then, I never inherited that kind of persistence from my mom.

Sometimes you wonder how weak and hollow people become without it showing on outer side. How can they just end a life so precious, just because they realize that the only way they were banking upon to make a luxurious living is closed now? Yeah… my brother in law committed suicide. It evokes pity from me, for his parents, a secret and yet little elation for my upset sister, an extreme depression for my nephew clubbed with unlimited worry and apathy for one, who left it all behind. I don’t intend to speak ill off who is gone, but he had done his share to instill this hatred in me, for HIM.

I have met few other friends on my way to where I am. I have changed radically from someone, who was quite introvert, apprehensive and unsure to someone who doesn’t care, sure of what he wants and confident person. You can always count on your life to teach you all the important lessons in crudest and cruelest of ways. This is the part, which was probably most drastic and striking [I would rather say dramatic] in my life, yet I feel that, skipping over that one year, would still make me feel more comfortable. Something’s are just not meant to be talked.

More things have happened in middle of all this. Things that qualify to be mentioned, and yet too secretive to be said. After all, somewhere inside, I still have that “closed” me, wandering still.

My family; a man, who never gave up on life. A dignified woman who made quite a few hasty and wrong decisions, but can’t be held responsible for them. She stands in a place of respect, where no one else ever will. A young mother, who has courage to stand against world for what she believes in, who will fight for her deserved acceptance and respect. I don’t know, which of these traits I have. All I know is that I have “hope”. You know what they say about hope?
“Hope is one of the good things, probably best of the things and good things never die! ~ Shawshank Redemption”.

I have written this blog for few noted reasons. First, because being my friend, you have whole right to share an insight in my life, but I would much appreciate that if it stays between us. You must realize that it is something that I have shared with you after much thought and re-re-re-reconsideration. Secondly, it is not out of self-pity that I have summarized my life, instead, I wanted to archive all the grueling days, so that when in future I look back and read it, I can say, “You have come a long way. God must really love you!” :-D
And thirdly, to mark it as a day, whereon I will strive harder than ever to make sure, that I can be a man enough to stand by my parents against all those who think, it is easy to fuck with my family and get away with it. :-

I am the son, my parents lost as their first child, four months after he was born. And I will do anything to match up the expectations my parents would have had from him, if he was still here. I know my mom secretly miss him, but she wouldn’t tell me.

It runs in my family, and we never give up. If you ever want to know anything about my family, you must look into the eyes; eyes of my dad, which always speak of helplessness and love. Eyes of my mom, immense faith and will to go on; to stand up against anyone and anything for her kids, for her family and for anything that means to her. Eyes of my sister; speaking of all the hope clinging on the brim, hope for herself and hope all the good things for her son. And my eyes, yeah… well, they are always digging into you, trying to find out if there is a split “you” hiding inside you too.
This is my life, for all those who always wondered what’s behind that crazy laugh? Hope all your questions have been answered today! :-D

Well, below this you will find loads of junk, written over years and years! Timestamps are all new, because i shifted to new blog sometime back! :-D They are few selected ones from recent past. Most of the saga is buried and decaying somewhere in this mammoth world of limitless information.
